claims.explanation: AZD7762 is a CHK1/CHK2 inhibitor that selectively kills tumor cells with a defective G1 DNA-damage checkpoint, forcing reliance on CHK1-dependent G2 arrest and homologous recombination for survival. TP53 mutation (and other G1 checkpoint lesions) therefore sensitizes, while intact p53 or intact HR (e.g., BRCA2, ATM) protects. The pattern is consistent with p53-mutant, HR-deficient, and replication-stress-prone lineages being most affected.

features.basis: Loss of G1 checkpoint creates reliance on CHK1/G2; p53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive list (PMID 22446188, 20233881)
HR deficiency plus CHK1 inhibition impairs DNA repair (PMID 20501833)
BRCA2-mutant lines appear among least affected, suggesting intact residual HR or context-dependent resistance
ATM loss impairs DNA damage signaling and increases dependence on CHK1 (PMID 20501833)
Higher CHK1 expression/activity supports G2 arrest and survival; NSCLC stem cells show strong Chk1 activation (PMID 22117197)
AZD7762 inhibits Rad51 focus formation; high HR capacity protects (PMID 20501833)
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via replication stress
PTEN loss appears in several sensitive lines and may impair DNA repair
SWI/SNF loss is enriched in sensitive lines and may increase replication stress
ARID1A loss appears in sensitive lines and may impair chromatin-based repair
CDKN2A loss disrupts G1 control, increasing reliance on CHK1
MDM2 amplification would attenuate p53 and mimic checkpoint loss, but intact p53 pathway can protect
